alex: Quick triage thread — ran a micro-profiling sweep for the host-side path on canary traffic, focusing on short chat requests (<= 64 tokens). Seeing host overhead dominate 25-40% of request CPU. Flame attached inlined below.
maria: Can you paste the profiler summary? numbers matter here.
alex: Summary from pprof (sampled, 60s):
```
tokenize_and_parse         28.4%
request_deserialize        18.1%
grpc_writev/syscalls       10.9%
stream_chunk_assemble      8.7%
kernel_dispatch_overhead   6.2%
kv_cache_miss_handling     5.4%
other/idle                 22.3%
```
jamal: Huh — KV miss handling shows up even for short requests? are we mis-tagging misses as cold or is eviction noise spiking?
cheng: I think the gRPC path is paying for many small writev syscalls when streaming tokens. We still flush per-chunk on the host. That syscall tail adds up on CPU and latency.
riya: Do we have an easy knob to coalesce small frames before write? Or adjust chunk size on the host-side framer?
alex: We can increase coalesce window from 4ms -> 12ms in the framer as an experiment; tradeoff = +burst latency for fewer syscalls. Also consider writev batching at the socket layer.
maria: Also check parsing: the request_deserialize step includes JSON->proto conversion and our tokenization call. Could we move tokenization into a shared threadpool or offload to the runtime process pinned to a different core?
jamal: KV-cache correlation: during the sweep I saw 2x miss rate when incoming seq lengths vary a lot. Our cache key includes model+prefix fingerprint; we might be over-fragmenting the cache with micro-prefixes.
cheng: On kernel selection: for short sequences the current selector picks the high-throughput kernel which assumes larger effective batch sizes. For tiny micro-batches that gives worse tail latency — should bias selector towards lower-latency kernels below batch threshold.
riya: Proposed immediate fixes (small safe experiments):
  - framer: coalesce window 4ms -> 12ms (canary).
  - kernel selector: add branch: if batch_size<=8 and seq_len<=64 prefer low-latency kernel.
  - tokenization: enable shared pool worker for tokenize calls (limit concurrency).
  - kvcache: normalize prefix keys by dropping last-k tokens for short requests (reduce fragmentation).

alex: I'll open canaries for framer and kernel selector changes. I'll also add a quick benchmark harness for tokenization offload.

maria: Sounds good. Add measurement hooks: per-request syscall_count, tokenization_latency, kv_cache_hit boolean, kernel_choice tag.
oncall-bot: Deploy started: ingress-framer-coalesce canary -> hosts rg-us-east-3 (build 2026.03.17-ff2). Watch alerts on latency/slo.
jamal: Follow-up: if coalescing causes >8ms p50 regressions, we should instead try writev batching in the runtime worker (reduce syscall frequency but keep framing latency low).
cheng: I'll prototype a writev-buffering layer that aggregates up to 8KB or 8ms, whichever comes first. Should avoid reordering with streaming semantics.
riya: I'll add a perf dashboard tile: host_overhead.tokenize+parse, host_overhead.syscalls, kvcache.hit_rate for the canary group.
alex: Action items: alex -> land kernel selector guard + benchmark (ETA end of day), cheng -> prototype writev-batcher (ETA 48h), riya -> dashboard + perf hooks (ETA 24h), jamal -> kv key normalization test (ETA 48h).

maria: Thanks — aim to reconvene after 48h with numbers. If the canary looks good we'll roll to 10% and then 50%.
alex: Copy. Will post perf diffs here. :thumbsup:
